newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco reports progress on Century.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco reports progress on Century.

text.p: The world's largest zinc producer, Pasminco Ltd, said on Wednesday negotiations were progressing with Aboriginal groups over the development of the A$1 billion Century zinc mine in the state of Queensland.

"Six claimants representing the local communities have reached agreement with CZL (Century Zinc Ltd), however two further groups of claimants comprising six individuals have yet to reach agreement," the company said in a statement.
Only four claimants had agreed to the mine when the parties decided on February 14 to go to arbitration after the closure of a deadline set by RTZ-CRA, the project owners.

In January, Pasminco said it would buy the CZL and Dugald River zinc projects from RTZ-CRA for A$345 million conditional on the Queensland government issuing mining leases which depend on CZL and Aborginal groups resolving the current impasse.
The talks are focussed on land rights under Australia's Native Title legislation and over the A$60 million compensation and jobs package offered to Aborigines affected by the project.
Pasminco said arbitration would begin shortly and might take up to six months.
The company earlier reported a net profit of A$20.2 million, for the six months to December 31, unchanged from the same period in 1995.
